purpose: How much of a survey displacement follows the guide direction?
meaning: Normalize the nonzero reference direction with a scaled norm, take the dot product with that unit direction, and multiply back by the unit direction. Subtract to obtain the orthogonal residual.

definition.setting: A survey displacement is resolved along a chosen nonzero reference direction. Keep the parallel part separate from the perpendicular residual.
definition.formal_latex: c=\frac{\vec u\cdot\vec v}{\|\vec v\|},\quad\operatorname{proj}_{\vec v}\vec u=\frac{\vec u\cdot\vec v}{\vec v\cdot\vec v}\vec v,\quad\vec r=\vec u-\operatorname{proj}_{\vec v}\vec u,\quad\vec r\cdot\vec v=0.
conditions: A survey displacement is resolved along a chosen nonzero reference direction. Keep the parallel part separate from the perpendicular residual.

The reference vector must be nonzero. Multiplying it by a positive factor leaves the projection unchanged, while reversing it reverses the signed scalar component and preserves the projection vector. The residual is orthogonal to the reference; projection is not the full displacement.
All values use the declared frame and units. Numerical positions and magnitudes are floating-point evaluations; an underflowed nonzero product is reported as a precision failure.
